summary.text: A 59-year-old woman was admitted with abdominal pain for a year and rectal bleeding for a month. Colonoscopy found a scirrhous tumor mass on the sigmoid colon with otherwise normal mucosa, CT showed rectosigmoid wall thickening and millimetric lymph nodes, and biopsy was reported as colorectal carcinoma.

Low anterior resection was performed, with a pathological diagnosis of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with intact borders, T3N0M0. Oral capecitabine 3 gm/day for 14 days per month was administered.

Two months later she was admitted with bloody diarrhea about 10 times a day; fever and tachycardia were found, and stool showed abundant leukocytes and erythrocytes without parasitic cysts or ova. Capecitabine was stopped and intravenous ciprofloxacin and metronidazole were given, but symptoms had not resolved on the seventh day. Repeat colonoscopy showed hyperemic, edematous, fragile and erosive colonic mucosa, biopsy was compatible with chronic active colitis, and ulcerative pancolitis with severe activation was diagnosed.

Clinical remission was achieved with oral mesalazine, mesalazine enema and metilprednisolone; metilprednisolone was then tapered and stopped, and mesalazine was chosen for maintenance. Colonoscopy one year after resection showed normal colonic mucosa with no recurrence of colorectal carcinoma.

ambiguities.issue: The body diagnosis sentence is worded "was considered as"; it is recorded as confirmed because it is the authors' final diagnosis, stated without hedging in the case abstract and followed by induction and maintenance therapy. The discussion hedges the cause (resection, capecitabine, perioperative stress or underlying silent colitis).

evidence.quote: Diagnosis was considered as ulcerative pan colitis with severe clinical and endoscopic activation.
have been developed ulcerative colitis 2 months after low anterior resection and oral capecitabine treatment
It is unclear which role is certain.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that capecitabine or resection caused the colitis, or that the colitis was a pre-existing silent disease.

ambiguities.issue: The case sentence does not state the capecitabine setting. The discussion contrasts the case's "adjuvant chemotherapy regimen" with the literature but does not name capecitabine, so the setting stays unknown. The order of resection and capecitabine is not stated in the case text.

evidence.quote: Oral capecitabine 3 gm/day for 14 days per month was administered.

Except adjuvant chemotherapy regimen, the case we present; location of the tumor, interval for development of ulcerative colitis and surgical procedure for treatment of colorectal carcinoma were similar with the cases described in literature.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not add an adjuvant setting, a start date, or a resection-before-capecitabine order to the capecitabine course.

ambiguities.issue: Hemoglobin, white blood cell and platelet values are placed in a parenthesis in the sentence about unresolved symptoms on the seventh day of treatment; no flags are stated.
